title: token-boundary-shimming-and-kvcache-proposal
content:
Summary
------
This is a working proposal for a lightweight "shim" layer at the tokenizer/runtime boundary to: (1) reduce end-to-end tail latency for short requests by allowing speculative scheduling, (2) surface cache-friendly hints for KV-cache keying and prefetching, and (3) expose minimal metadata for smarter batching decisions without tightly coupling the runtime to a concrete tokenizer implementation.

Context and motivation
----------------------
We frequently see tokenization time dominate for small prompts (single-sentence user chat) especially on CPU-hosted tokenizer workers. Current flow is: accept request -> run tokenizer (blocking) -> hand token ids into runtime -> runtime queues and batches. This rigid handoff creates two problems:
- head-of-line blocking when a long tokenization-run delays many short requests behind it
- inability for runtime to pre-warm KV cache or pick an appropriate kernel until token ids are visible

We need a contract that:
- keeps tokenizer implementations pluggable (fastBPE, sentencepiece, byte-level fallback),
- gives runtime enough signal early to (a) decide batch window length, (b) start KV-cache lookups or prefetch, (c) trigger model-variant fallback if tokenization reveals long sequences, and
- enables opportunistic micro-batching of tokenizers themselves.

Proposal: token-boundary shim API
--------------------------------
Introduce a two-phase lightweight tokenization handshake between API/front-end and the serving runtime. Shim exposes 3 small RPCs (or calls in-process) with clear latency budgets:

1) preflight_hint(request_meta) -> preflight_response
   - input (small): request_meta {client_id, model_hint, explicit_max_tokens, prefer_latency}
   - output: preflight_response {predicted_encoding, tokenizer_variant_hint, expect_token_count_estimate, cache_prefix_hash_hint, deadline_ms_for_tokenizer}
   - semantics: non-binding estimate a tokenizer can produce without doing full tokenization; implemented by fast heuristics (character count -> token estimate, model vocab sampling) so it returns quickly.

2) encode_stream(request_text, options) -> encoded_chunk*(stream) + final_ids
   - streaming encode: tokenizer may emit encoded chunks of token ids as they become available (e.g., after each sentence or segment). Runtime can start KV-cache checks on early chunks.
   - chunks are idempotent and must include a sequence offset.
   - fallback: tokenizer can signal "slow_encode" and runtime can decide to route to higher-priority worker or use a byte-level fallback.

3) cache_key_hint(token_prefix_metadata) -> cache_key_str
   - a canonicalized hint that the tokenizer can compute cheaply (hash of normalized string + model id + encoder settings). Runtime consumes this to create or probe KV-cache entries before final ids are delivered.

Why streaming + preflight helps
-----------------------------
- Short requests: preflight gives runtime a fast signal to start kernel selection and batch-window sizing (choose minimal batching, low-latency path).
- Medium requests: early encoded chunks allow KV cache prefetch so that by the time full decode begins, common prefixes are already hot in GPU memory.
- Long requests: tokenizer can mark as "long" early so scheduler picks a throughput-optimized worker and can activate quantized kernels.

KV-cache key conventions (proposal)
----------------------------------
Design goal: stable, deterministic keys that avoid collisions across tokenizer variants and minor normalization differences. Key components (all concatenated with a single delimiter and hashed):
- model_family:vX (e.g., redwood-7B:v1)
- tokenizer_fingerprint (sha1 of tokenizer vocab + config)
- normalized_prefix_hash (normalized text -> lowercased + NFKC + collapse spaces; then sha1)
- tokenization_options_hash (e.g., special tokens, add_bos flag)
- prompt_length_bucket (tiny/short/medium/long)
Example key (pre-hash): redwood-7B:v1|sp-2a3f...|norm-9b2...|opt-01|bucket-short 
Notes:
- Runtime should allow speculative lookup using cache_key_hint even if final token ids later differ by one token due to tokenizer variant; we accept occasional misses but avoid harmful collisions.
- New experiments: lightweight key that excludes tokenizer_fingerprint for loose hits (lower cost, more false positives).

Scheduler interactions and batching implications
----------------------------------------------
- Batching window adapts to preflight estimate: prefer a small non-zero micro-window for low-latency clients (e.g., 1-5ms) and longer windows for high throughput/policy.
- Tokenization can itself be batched: implement a tokenization worker pool that accepts multiple texts and runs vectorized BPE ops when beneficial. Shim's preflight_hint can be used to group similar-shaped tokenizations into the same micro-batch.
- When encode_stream emits early chunks, runtime should be able to assign those to an "early KV probe" pipeline that runs asynchronously and primes GPU memory without blocking scheduling decisions.

Failure and fallback modes
--------------------------
- If preflight_hint times out or is missing, default to conservative low-latency scheduling (avoid long batching).
- If tokenizer errors, runtime should have a fallback tokenizer (byte-level) with a clear signal back to the API for degraded output quality.
- If a KV-cache prefetch fails (timeout or eviction), runtime continues without it; correctness must not depend on the cache.

Observability and instrumentation
--------------------------------
Expose these metrics at taggable levels (per-route, per-client, per-model):
- tokenizer.preflight_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- tokenizer.encode_chunk_latency_ms
- tokenizer.full_encode_latency_ms
- fraction_of_requests_with_streamed_chunks
- kvcache.probe_latency_ms and kvcache.prefetch_hit_ratio
- scheduler.batching_window_ms chosen per-request
Trace events: preflight.start, preflight.end, encode.chunk.n, kvcache.prefetch.start, model.kernels.selected.

Open questions / tradeoffs
-------------------------
- How much effort to put into tokenizer_fingerprint stability? Rolling tokenizer changes will invalidate cache; need versioning strategy.
- Security: hints leak normalized prefix hashes. For privacy-sensitive workloads we should allow opt-out of prefetch/cache hints.
- Complexity vs benefit: streaming encode adds complexity to every tokenizer; evaluate if preflight-only + a cheap prefix-hash is 'good enough' for most cases.

Small experiment plan (MVPs)
---------------------------
1) Quick win (2 weeks): implement preflight_hint in fronting layer + runtime logic to choose micro-batch window. Measure delta on p95 latency for short chat requests.
2) Medium (4–6 weeks): add cache_key_hint generation and speculative KV prefetch for prefix-short requests. Track prefetch hit ratio and end-to-end latency improvements.
3) Longer (8+ weeks): implement encode_stream in tokenizer pool and runtime early-chunk pipeline; implement tokenization micro-batching in tokenizer pool.

Implementation notes / compatibility
----------------------------------
- Keep shim backwards-compatible: runtime should accept both old flow (blocking tokenizer -> ids) and new shim flow.
- Tokenizer SDK: provide a small reference shim library (python + go) that implements preflight_hint and streamable encode. Keep binary compatibility with current tokenizer containers.

Appendix: example sequence (short chat)
--------------------------------------
1. request arrives with model_hint=redwood-7B, prefer_latency=true
2. preflight_hint returns expect_token_count_estimate=~8, cache_prefix_hash_hint=abc123, deadline_ms_for_tokenizer=15
3. runtime picks low-latency kernel, sets batch_window=3ms, kicks off kvcache.probe(cache_prefix=abc123) asynchronously
4. tokenizer quickly emits encode_stream chunk 1 (tokens for first sentence) -> runtime applies early KV results to warm prefix
5. tokenizer final_ids arrive; runtime merges warmed state and proceeds to generation with lower token cache misses

Notes / Todos
------------
- [ ] Draft tokenizer shim proto (RPC definitions) and share with tokenizer owners
- [ ] Add privacy opt-out field to preflight_hint
- [ ] Run microbenchmarks for character->token heuristics accuracy
- [ ] Simulate micro-batching gain with synthetic traces

Contact
-------
For questions, ping Asha Patel (owner) or Miguel Santos on #serving-runtime.

This doc is intentionally informal and iterative — aiming to collect feedback from tokenizer implementers and runtime schedulers before updating to a formal design spec.
